en.title: Minimize Path Value
en.description: You are given a weighted undirected graph, a start node source, and an end node destination. The stress level of a path is the maximum edge weight on the path; find the path with the minimum stress level. If the two nodes are not connected, return -1. If source=destination, return 0, consistent with the three fixed source implementations.
en.input: The first line contains N M; each of the next M lines contains u v w; the last line contains source destination. Nodes are numbered 1..N. Constraints added by this site: 1≤N≤5000, 0≤M≤20000, 1≤u,v,source,destination≤N, 0≤w≤10^9. The upstream Constraints section is a corrupted placeholder, so the sizes above and the non-negative weight range are bounds stated explicitly by this site; the graph is not required to be connected, and parallel edges and self-loops are allowed.
en.output: Output one integer: the minimum possible maximum edge weight along a path, or -1 if destination is unreachable. Output 0 when source=destination.
en.explanation: Maintain the minimum bottleneck value from source across the graph. When extending u→v, the stress of the new path is max(current stress, w). Use a priority queue and each time finalize the node with the smallest current bottleneck value.
hints: Define the path state as the minimum possible maximum edge weight on reaching a node, not the path length.
